biomarkers.name: Chromogranin A, synaptophysin, S100 (sustentacular)
biomarkers.prevalence: Synaptophysin is typically diffuse/strong; chromogranin is commonly positive but can be variable; S100 highlights sustentacular cells in many cases, often reduced or absent in high-grade tumors
biomarkers.clinical_use: Confirms neuroendocrine/neural differentiation and sustentacular pattern supportive of olfactory neuroblastoma

biomarkers.name: SSTR2 (somatostatin receptor 2)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Imaging (68Ga-DOTATATE PET) and potential PRRT (177Lu-DOTATATE) in selected recurrent/metastatic cases �theranostic approach

biomarkers.name: IDH2 R172
biomarkers.prevalence: Recurrent in a subset; enriched in higher-grade tumors
biomarkers.clinical_use: Molecular finding reported in olfactory neuroblastoma; supportive of disease biology rather than established routine clinical selection

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Lobular architecture of small round blue cells with fibrillary neuropil, Homer-Wright rosettes (pseudorosettes) and occasional Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (true rosettes)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Hyams grading (I-IV) based on architecture, mitoses, necrosis, pleomorphism, differentiation

tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Sustentacular cells (S100+) at periphery of lobules �characteristic

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Olfactory neuroepithelial basal progenitor cells are the leading proposed cell of origin, but this remains unproven
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Recapitulates olfactory neuroepithelial/neuroblastic differentiation �Homer-Wright rosettes support neuroblastic differentiation; Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes can occur but are not a marker of mature olfactory differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Hyams grade reflects differentiation state �grade I is well differentiated and grade IV poorly differentiated/undifferentiated
